body:
mira: quick question — bringing up llamaX-q8 on h100x2 pools in us-west and eu-west. during a 2k rps burst eu-west shows 25-40ms tail increases with FlashAttention v3, us-west is fine. should we add a per-region fallback to Triton kernels or vendor libs? :thinking:

devon: can you paste the perf logs? curious if it's kernel warm-up or NV driver differences across regions.

mira: logs below (snippet):
```
[2026-03-18T15:02:12Z] region=eu-west model=llamaX-q8 kernel=flashv3 qps=2200 p99=42ms p95=18ms
[2026-03-18T15:02:12Z] region=us-west model=llamaX-q8 kernel=flashv3 qps=2300 p99=16ms p95=10ms
[2026-03-18T15:02:13Z] region=eu-west kernel=tcmalloc mem_frag=0.28
```

lina: eww, mem_frag high in eu-west. last time that happened it was a driver+cuda patch that changed allocation patterns and made FlashAttn v3's kernel tiling worse on our AMI. vendor libs seemed unaffected.

paul: two quick levers: 1) fallback policy based on regional p99 over threshold, 2) progressive switch (canary 10% -> 50% -> 100%). avoid global flips.

mira: thinking policy like this:
```
fallback_policy:
  per_region:
    eu-west:
      trigger: p99 > 30ms for 5m
      sequence: [triton-autotuned, vendor-sm90, flashv2]
      rollout: 10,50,100
    default:
      trigger: p99 > 50ms
      sequence: [flashv2, triton-autotuned]
      rollout: 100
```

devon: looks fine. add a cooldown window (10m) and ensure cache invalidation for KV cache when kernel changes — we saw stale KV pointers if we flip too fast.

paul: also measure tokens/sec and linearize p99 vs. batch size. Triton-autotuned helps throughput but can hurt small-batch latency. vendor-sm90 was better at small batches in our SLO tests.

benchmark-bot: perf-report attached (summary): eu-west flashv3 p99=38ms throughput=95k tok/s; eu-west vendor-sm90 p99=22ms throughput=88k tok/s; us-west flashv3 p99=15ms throughput=102k tok/s. Quantized Q8 accuracy delta ~= 0.6% vs FP16 baseline.

lina: given accuracy delta small, fallback to vendor-sm90 in eu-west seems reasonable. prefer staged canary and monitor quality regression on prompt-set A.

mira: agree. i'll push a canary to 10% in eu-west with cooldown and KV cache bounce. also adding logging hooks to track kernel-specific mem usage.

deploy-bot: rolling canary: region=eu-west pool=llamaX-q8 percent=10 -> started at 2026-03-18T15:10:00Z

devon: keep an eye on GC/fragmentation. if we see mem_frag > 0.25 consistently, escalate to infra to rebuild AMI or pin driver.

mira: noted. last q: when do we prefer flashv2 over triton-autotuned generally? any concrete heuristics?

paul: heuristics we use: if median latency < 8ms and load is steady, flashv3 is preferred (best throughput). If tail p99 jumps under burst or mem_frag > 0.2, prefer triton-autotuned for stability. vendor libs are fallback for small-batch, high-concurrency noisy neighbors. flashv2 is a safe fallback when flashv3 regresses after kernel-level changes (less aggressive optimizations).

lina: add to runbook: "If p99 delta between regions > 1.5x, enable per-region kernel overrides instead of global rules". helps avoid chasing noisy neighbors.

mira: perfect. i'll update the policy yaml and run the canary. will post results in ~30m. thanks all :thumbsup:

benchmark-bot: canary summary (T+30m): eu-west 10% vendor-sm90 p99=21ms -> stabilized, no quality regression on eval set A.

mira: rollback trigger clear. expanding to 50% now.

deploy-bot: canary update: region=eu-west percent=50 -> started at 2026-03-18T15:45:00Z

paul: fyi, file a short postmortem if we decide to rebuild AMI/drivers so infra has context.

mira: will do.
